newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico oilseed crushing plant fight goes on--paper.
newsitem.headline: Mexico oilseed crushing plant fight goes on--paper.

text.p: National Association of Copra Producers (UNPC) is pressing its case for the return of an oilseed and coconut meat crushing plant in the southern state of Tabasco, the daily El Financiero said Wednesday.

Jose Antonio Tejeda Garcia, the head of the coconut meat producing group, told El Financiero that the three-year battle over the ownership rights of the Oleaginosas del Sureste plant continues and he expects the UNPC to win the case.
The UNPC claims government officials illegally sold off the plant to Grupo Aceitero Mexicano and for a price below its real value.
Officials from the company and the Tabsaco state government were not immediately available for comment. Wednesday is a holiday in Mexico for Constitution Day.
The Tabasco state government took over the plant from the 14,000-member UNPC alleging it was being run "in the red" and was technically bankrupt.
UNCP leaders claim state officials falsified balance sheets to give the appearance of bankruptcy and then sold it to Grupo Aceitera Mexicano "under the table," El Financiero said.
